hook: The dictator who made the Soviet Union a superpower at the cost of millions of lives.

pages.x: Ioseb Jughashvili was born in 1878 in Gori, in Georgia, the son of a shoemaker who beat him. Smallpox scarred his face. He trained to be a priest, but turned to revolution.

As a revolutionary he organised strikes and robberies to raise money for the Bolsheviks. He was arrested and exiled to Siberia again and again, and escaped again and again. He took the name Stalin, "man of steel".
After Lenin's death in 1924, Stalin, the party's general secretary, outwitted his rivals, among them Trotsky, and by 1929 ruled alone.

He forced the country to build steel mills, dams and cities at breakneck speed, and drove the peasants into collective farms. The famine that followed in 1932 and 1933 killed millions, above all in Ukraine and Kazakhstan.

In 1937 and 1938 his secret police arrested more than a million people. Some 700,000 were shot, among them most of the army's generals and many of his old comrades. Millions more were sent to labour camps, the Gulag.

In 1939 he made a pact with Hitler and they carved up Eastern Europe. In 1941 Hitler attacked anyway. The Soviet Union lost some 27 million people, but after Stalingrad its Red Army fought all the way to Berlin.
After 1945 he put communist governments in power across Eastern Europe, and in 1949 the Soviet Union tested its first atomic bomb. The Cold War with the West had begun.
He died after a stroke in 1953; his guards had been too afraid to enter his room for hours. In 1956 his successor, Khrushchev, denounced his crimes.

Stalin made the Soviet Union an industrial and military superpower that helped defeat Nazi Germany, at the cost of millions of lives in famine, executions and camps. He was one of the deadliest dictators in history.
pts: Ruled the Soviet Union from the late 1920s to 1953
Millions died in his famines, purges and camps
